title: Issue Closing QA
eyebrow: QA · #361 issue closing: the agent closes issues itself, under a guard · house-rules 2.70.0

short.lead: Issue closing (#361) is built on the branch AjsAgent/issue-281-fix as house-rules 2.70.0. The agent now closes an issue itself, but only with evidence on record: your QA pass and a merge to main, or a list you approved. The guard is a check that runs before any command that closes an issue. It refuses every other close and says what evidence is missing. verify.py, the script that checks the hooks do what the docs say, passed on two runs, each with 913 checks. A live run on this repo refused a close of #307 by both routes: a gh command (GitHub's command-line tool) and the GitHub tool this session uses.
short.hint: Tap a row to see what was built and how it was checked.
items: When you pass QA on a feature, its issues are saved in a list called closable, in the design loop's stage file, .claude/house-rules-loop.json.
That list now survives when you approve the next design. Before this change, approving the next design erased the recorded issues.

When a pull request merges, every entry waiting in the closable list is marked with that pull request's number. This happens only with proof of the merge: the GitHub tool reporting it merged, gh exiting with code 0 (success), or gh printing its "merged pull request" line. An auto-merge that has not happened yet marks nothing.
Nothing from you. Checked by 10 verify.py cases.
A close goes through only with a QA pass and a merge on record, or with your approval on a list.

Every other close is refused, and the refusal names what is missing. This covers both routes: gh commands, and the GitHub tool this session uses. The guard did not check the GitHub tool before this change.
The evidence is removed only after proof that the close succeeded, so a failed close can be retried.
Nothing from you. Checked by 22 verify.py cases and a live run on this repo.
A sweep is a review of open issues for closing. The sweep page lists each issue with its evidence and a suggested action, and records the closes it proposes.
Your reply "Sweep approved: issues" approves them; adding "keep #N" leaves #N open.
Your message "Close as not planned: #N replaced by #M" approves a not-planned close for the issues you name.
These phrases count only from you, never from a helper agent or a notification.
Nothing from you. Checked by 11 verify.py cases.
Rule 6 in rules/detail/issue-workflow.md and the short rule in rules/house-rules.md now state the new rule.
docs/4-systems/issue-closing.md describes the mechanism; the plugin is 2.70.0.
Read the new rule, then pass or fail QA
Read rule 6 in claude-house-rules/plugins/house-rules/rules/detail/issue-workflow.md and say whether it matches what you asked for.
Once you pass QA and the pull request merges, the issues of this feature (#361 to #365) are the first ones I close under the new guard, which is the real test.
The sweep page for the 124 open issues comes next.
Reply "QA passed: issue closing", or "QA failed: issue closing" and say what is wrong.

unverified: No Claude Code session has run house-rules 2.70.0 yet; the checks ran the branch's scripts directly, and the live run drove its hooks by hand
The real result shapes of a gh close and a gh merge in a live session are assumed from gh's own output text, and the guard falls back to refusing when it can't prove a success
The diff against main also counts this branch's plan pages, not only this feature's files

wrapup.summary: QA for issue closing (#361): the agent closes issues itself under a guard that checks your QA pass and the merge, house-rules 2.70.0.
wrapup.changing: Once you pass QA, a pull request takes 2.70.0 to main. Then the sweep page for the 124 open issues comes to you, and restructure step 2 (#340) resumes.
